record.paper_title: Selected open problems in Matching Under Preferences
record.original_question: Given a Stable Marriage instance I and a matching M_0, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether the divorce digraph D_I contains a directed path from the vertex v_{M_0} to a sink vertex, equivalently to some stable matching.

evidence.quote: This leads to a natural open question, namely to resolve the complexity of the following decision problem: given an sm instance I and a matching M0, is there a path in D_I from v_M0 to a sink vertex?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let I be an instance of the Stable Marriage problem: a set of n men and n women, each providing a strict, complete preference list over the members of the opposite sex. A matching M is a set of disjoint man–woman pairs that saturates everyone. A pair (m,w) ∉ M is a blocking pair of M if m prefers w to his partner in M and w prefers m to her partner in M; M is stable if it has no blocking pair.

Define the divorce digraph D_I as follows. Its vertices are all (perfect) matchings of I. For every matching M and every blocking pair (m,w) of M, place a directed arc from M to the matching M' obtained from M by "satisfying" (m,w), i.e., by pairing m with w and re-pairing their previous partners with each other (so M' differs from M only on these two pairs). The sinks of D_I are exactly the stable matchings of I.

Decision problem. Given as input a Stable Marriage instance I together with a (not necessarily stable) matching M_0 of I, determine the computational complexity of deciding whether D_I contains a directed path from the vertex M_0 to some sink, equivalently, whether some sequence of blocking-pair resolutions starting from M_0 reaches a stable matching.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent work on "paths to stability" for the stable marriage problem (including a 2023 paper on Improved Paths to Stability) continues to study reachability in the divorce digraph, but does not report a resolution of the complexity of deciding whether a given starting matching can reach a stable matching via blocking-pair resolutions. No source found that settles this decision problem; it appears still open.

status_evidence.title: Improved Paths to Stability for the Stable Marriage Problem
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithms that start from an arbitrary matching and iteratively resolve blocking pairs to reach a stable matching; complexity questions on the divorce digraph remain studied.
status_evidence.claim: Recent literature continues to study divorce-digraph reachability without settling the decision complexity.

status_evidence.title: Divorce Digraph -- from Wolfram MathWorld
status_evidence.snippet: A divorce digraph encodes blocking-pair resolutions among matchings; stable matchings are its sinks.
status_evidence.claim: Defines the divorce digraph used in the problem.

status_evidence.title: Paths to marriage stability
status_evidence.snippet: Studies sequences of blocking-pair resolutions leading to stable matchings.
status_evidence.claim: Background work on paths to stability without resolving the stated decision complexity.
